steps.title: Trace a stopped starter

quiz.prompt: Does development status three certify an arithmetic answer?

choices.text: Only for a zero exponent.
No; it marks unfinished work.
Yes, if the low byte happens to match.

hints.text: Identify the function boundary and which state is numerical data.
An unfinished return is observable without claiming a completed arithmetic value.

steps.expectedObservation: An unfinished return is observable without claiming a completed arithmetic value.
steps.prose: Open the cumulative starter and locate the seven entry points and their marked regions. The default caller selects the gcd example. Missing regions return development status three; the gcd also uses v1 to distinguish this from a numerical answer. Run to the caller's return before interpreting output. The result objects begin with sentinels.

steps.expectedObservation: The pair reaches1 and0 after the divisions shown earlier.

steps.prose: Use the four Euclidean divisions to substitute backwards from remainder one. Keep the signed coefficients separate from the unsigned gcd values. Verify17 times2753 equals15 times3120 plus one before using those fixed exponents in the toy calculation.

steps.prose: Use base fffffffe, exponent two and modulus ffffffff in the scalar routine. The widened square has bit63 set. Compare the unsigned remainder with the signed interpretation worked earlier, then inspect the four output bytes. This case distinguishes arithmetic interpretations that small toy values cannot.

steps.title: Establish a valid modular-addition entry

hints.text: Carry and unsigned comparison are separate reasons to subtract.

steps.expectedObservation: For1 plus1 modulo17, the low result remains two at the done boundary.

steps.title: Propagate the subtraction borrow

steps.prose: Return to the OAEP and PSS discussion after the numerical routines agree. The toy modular power supplies no message encoding or signature verification scheme. Retain this distinction when describing the completed project, and keep any later key-generation or scheme work under a separate contract.
